title: Before the moment
subtitle: A six-round story about protection, assumptions, and different preferences.
setting: You are Jordan, spending an evening at Sam's apartment. You are both adult college students and have started talking about having sex. You want barrier protection to be part of the plan, but you are nervous about bringing it up.

characters.name: Jordan
characters.description: You play Jordan, who wants to state a protection boundary without making the conversation feel like an accusation.

characters.name: Sam
characters.description: Jordan's partner, who has their own preferences, questions, and assumptions about the evening.

goal: Talk clearly about protection, repair a misunderstanding, and decide what to do when preferences or practical plans differ.

start.title: Bringing it up
start.situation: The conversation is turning toward sex. You want barrier protection to be part of the plan, but you worry that raising the topic will change the mood.
start.partner: I'm really enjoying tonight. Would you like to stay a little longer?
start.prompt: How do you start the protection conversation?

choices.label: I'd like that. If we're thinking about sex, could we talk about protection first?
choices.response: Sure. What were you thinking?
choices.explanation: You separate staying together from deciding to have sex. Naming the topic now gives both people time to think.

choices.label: I'd like to. We should probably be careful, though.
choices.response: Sure. What do you mean by being careful?
choices.explanation: This can feel like an easier opening when you are shy. The word 'careful' leaves your actual condition unstated, so clarification matters.

specific_question.title: Naming your condition
specific_question.situation: Sam is ready to hear what you mean. You can state your own preference or fall back on what you assume they should know.

choices.label: I'd feel comfortable having sex if we use condoms or other barriers. How do you feel about that?
choices.response: Can I ask—are you worried I might have an STI?
choices.explanation: You make your condition specific and personal. Sam's response introduces a misunderstanding about your intention, rather than changing your right to that boundary.

choices.label: I thought you'd already know what I meant about protection.
choices.response: Oh. I feel a little judged by that. I was just trying to understand what you meant.
choices.explanation: You assume Sam should already know what you mean instead of saying what you need. You can repair the tone and still keep the same protection boundary.

vague_question.title: Careful can mean different things
vague_question.situation: Sam has asked for specifics. This is a chance to replace a general hint with a clear statement.
vague_question.partner: Sure. What do you mean by being careful?

choices.label: I mean condoms or other barriers. I got a little shy saying it out loud.
choices.response: Can I ask—are you worried I might have an STI?
choices.explanation: You correct the ambiguity without making a claim about Sam's health. Clear language can still bring up feelings that need a separate response.

choices.label: I'm probably overthinking it. I'm sure it'll be fine.
choices.response: Oh, so are you saying you're okay without barriers?
choices.explanation: Backing away may reduce awkwardness for a moment while leaving your needs hidden. Sam is now checking whether your reassurance means you are okay without barriers.

trust_misunderstanding.title: A boundary is not a diagnosis
trust_misunderstanding.situation: Sam hears your request as a judgment about them. You can explain the request without debating or guessing anyone's health status.
trust_misunderstanding.partner: Can I ask—are you worried I might have an STI?
trust_misunderstanding.prompt: How do you bring the conversation back to your needs?

choices.label: I'm not assuming anything about your health. I only feel comfortable having sex with barriers.
choices.response: I see what you mean. To be honest, I'd rather not use barriers.
choices.explanation: You explain your intention and make the boundary independent of an assumption about Sam. Understanding your request does not guarantee that your preferences will match.

choices.label: It's about what helps me feel comfortable. I'm happy to talk it through, but I do need us to use barriers.
choices.response: I'd like to talk it through too. I have a few questions about the options, and I'm not ready to decide yet.
choices.explanation: You make room for questions without making your condition optional. The next step can be getting information rather than reaching an immediate decision.

judgment_repair.title: Repairing a sharp opening
judgment_repair.situation: Your wording sounded critical, and Sam has said so. You can acknowledge that without apologizing for wanting protection.
judgment_repair.partner: Oh. I feel a little judged by that. I was just trying to understand what you meant.
judgment_repair.prompt: How do you make the request clearer?

choices.label: Sorry, that sounded sharper than I meant. I only feel comfortable having sex with barriers.
choices.response: I see what you mean. To be honest, I'd rather not use barriers.
choices.explanation: You take responsibility for the tone and state the actual condition. A repaired conversation can still uncover a genuine disagreement.

choices.label: Sorry, I shouldn't have assumed. I'd like us to use barriers. Could we check what we have first?
choices.response: I'd be okay using barriers. I just don't think I have what we'd need here.
choices.explanation: You move from a judgment to a specific request and practical question. Agreement about protection is different from having the supplies to follow through.

agreement_assumed.title: Correcting an accidental yes
agreement_assumed.situation: Sam is checking what your vague reassurance meant. You can make your preference clear before either person acts on it.
agreement_assumed.partner: Oh, so are you saying you're okay without barriers?
agreement_assumed.prompt: What do you actually want to say?

choices.label: Actually, I got a little awkward and didn't say what I meant. I do want us to use barriers.
choices.response: I see what you mean. To be honest, I'd rather not use barriers.
choices.explanation: You name the misunderstanding and your present choice. You are allowed to correct an unclear answer rather than stay with someone else's interpretation.

choices.label: I was nervous saying it, but I do want barriers. Could we check what we'd need before going further?
choices.response: I'd be okay using barriers. I just don't think I have what we'd need here.
choices.explanation: You replace reassurance with a concrete condition and next step. Checking supplies does not commit you to having sex afterward.

different_preference.title: Your preferences do not match
different_preference.situation: Sam understands the request but does not share your preference. You do not need to convince Sam to want the same thing, and you do not need to give up your boundary.
different_preference.partner: I see what you mean. To be honest, I'd rather not use barriers.
different_preference.prompt: What can happen when there is no shared agreement?

choices.label: I understand. I still need barriers to feel comfortable, so I'd rather not have sex tonight.
choices.response: Okay, let's not have sex tonight. Would you like a little space?
choices.explanation: You accept that the preferences differ and make a decision consistent with your condition. Neither person has to give in for the conversation to end respectfully.

choices.label: I'd rather not have sex without them. Would you be up for just a movie, or would you rather call it a night?
choices.response: A movie sounds nice. And I'm happy for it to be just a movie.
choices.explanation: You offer a separate activity without treating it as compensation or a route back to sex. Both people can also choose to end the evening.

missing_supplies.title: Agreement meets a practical problem
missing_supplies.situation: You are both open to using barriers, but you do not have the supplies you would need. Your condition remains the same even if following the original plan is inconvenient.
missing_supplies.partner: I'd be okay using barriers. I just don't think I have what we'd need here.
missing_supplies.prompt: How do you adjust the plan?

choices.label: Then I'd rather not have sex tonight. I'd feel more comfortable waiting until we have what we need.
choices.response: Okay, let's not have sex tonight. Would you like a little space?
choices.explanation: You keep the practical obstacle separate from your willingness to change a condition. You can stop even when you both originally hoped to continue.

choices.label: I'd like to hold off on sex. Would you be up for just watching a movie instead?
choices.response: A movie sounds nice. And I'm happy for it to be just a movie.
choices.explanation: You suggest an alternative that does not depend on giving up your condition. A future possibility remains undecided rather than promised.

different_information_needs.title: A question does not need an instant answer
different_information_needs.situation: Sam wants more information before deciding. You also want your condition respected while those questions remain open.
different_information_needs.partner: I'd like to talk it through too. I have a few questions about the options, and I'm not ready to decide yet.
different_information_needs.prompt: What pace works for this conversation?

choices.label: Let's hold off on sex tonight. Maybe we could look at the UHS information when we're ready?
choices.response: I'd like that. We can look into it without figuring everything out tonight.
choices.explanation: You propose an information step with no immediate sexual decision attached. Individual health questions can be directed to an appropriate professional.

choices.label: We don't have to figure it all out tonight. I'd like a little time to think about my questions too.
choices.response: Okay, let's not have sex tonight. Would you like a little space?
choices.explanation: You allow both people to be uncertain and choose time rather than a rushed answer. A pause can be useful even before you have a complete list of questions.

plan_no_sex.title: Making the pause concrete
plan_no_sex.situation: You have agreed not to have sex tonight. You can leave the future open or plan a later conversation about needs and practical details.
plan_no_sex.partner: Okay, let's not have sex tonight. Would you like a little space?

choices.label: Yes, I think I'd like to head home. Let's leave any other plans for now.
choices.response: Okay. We can leave the rest for another day.
choices.explanation: You specify what taking space means for tonight. There is no requirement to offer a later encounter in exchange for having your boundary respected.

choices.label: A little space would help. Maybe another day we could talk about what we're both comfortable with?
choices.response: I'd be happy to talk. Is there anything you'd like us to start with?
choices.explanation: You suggest a future discussion rather than a future yes. A later conversation can still reveal that your conditions differ.

plan_company.title: Company is its own choice
plan_company.situation: Sam also likes the movie idea and understands that sex is off the table. You can accept that plan or notice that you would rather leave.
plan_company.partner: A movie sounds nice. And I'm happy for it to be just a movie.

choices.label: That sounds nice. Just the movie tonight, and either of us can call it a night whenever we want.
choices.response: Sounds good. Just the movie, and no worries if you decide you'd rather head home.
choices.explanation: You make the alternative specific and voluntary. Choosing company does not erase any earlier boundary.

choices.label: Actually, I think I'd feel better heading home. I'm glad we could talk, though.
choices.response: Okay. We can leave the rest for another day.
choices.explanation: You can revise an invitation after thinking about it. Gratitude for the conversation does not require you to stay.

plan_information.title: Learning without a promise
plan_information.situation: You have separated getting information from deciding to have sex. Now you can plan how to approach the questions without pressure.
plan_information.partner: I'd like that. We can look into it without figuring everything out tonight.
plan_information.prompt: How do you make that manageable?

choices.label: Maybe we could each think of our questions and check UHS or SHEP before we talk again?
choices.response: I'd be happy to talk. Is there anything you'd like us to start with?
choices.explanation: You identify trustworthy starting points and give each person space to think. Information can support a choice without obligating either person to make the same choice.

choices.label: I'd like to look into a few things on my own first. I'm not ready to plan another conversation just yet.
choices.response: Okay. We can leave the rest for another day.
choices.explanation: You can seek information privately and decide later whether to share it. A joint activity is an invitation, not a requirement.

decision_space.title: A complete stopping point
decision_space.situation: You are ready to leave with your protection boundary intact. You can close the evening or offer a later conversation without making a commitment to sex.
decision_space.partner: Okay. We can leave the rest for another day.
decision_space.prompt: What would you say before leaving?

choices.label: Thanks for listening. I think I'll head home and leave things here for now.
choices.response: Take care getting home.
choices.explanation: You finish with a clear present choice. A respectful ending does not require a solution to every difference between you.

choices.label: I'd like to talk about this again sometime, when we're both ready.
choices.response: Me too. We can just talk and see how we both feel.
choices.explanation: You leave room for learning more about each other's needs. The outcome of that conversation remains genuinely open.

decision_plan.title: A plan to talk, not a promise to proceed
decision_plan.situation: You are considering another discussion about protection. You can clarify its purpose or decide you need more time first.
decision_plan.partner: I'd be happy to talk. Is there anything you'd like us to start with?
decision_plan.prompt: How do you define the next conversation?

choices.label: Maybe what helps us each feel comfortable, and any questions we still have. Then we can see if we're on the same page.
choices.response: That sounds good. And it's okay if we still want different things.
choices.explanation: You make room for agreement and for continued disagreement. The goal is a voluntary choice, rather than persuading either person to drop a condition.

choices.label: Actually, I think I need a little more time before we talk about this again.
choices.response: Of course. There's no rush.
choices.explanation: You notice your own readiness and adjust the plan. You do not have to commit to another conversation simply because one was offered.

decision_company.title: Choosing a different evening
decision_company.situation: You and Sam have a concrete, shared movie plan with sex off the table. The last choice is whether you still want that company now.
decision_company.partner: Sounds good. Just the movie, and no worries if you decide you'd rather head home.

choices.label: I'd like to stay for the movie. I feel better now that we've talked.
choices.response: Me too. What are you in the mood to watch?
choices.explanation: You choose a mutually wanted activity on its own terms. It does not serve as an implied promise about later in the evening.

choices.label: That's kind of you. I think I'd feel better heading home after all, though.
choices.response: Of course. I'm glad you told me.
choices.explanation: You can decide against even a considerate plan. Changing your mind is part of making a voluntary choice.

ending_pause.title: The pause holds
ending_pause.summary: Jordan and Sam do not have sex tonight. Jordan keeps the protection boundary and leaves without promising a later encounter. Different preferences or unanswered questions can remain unresolved while both people's choices are respected.
takeaways: A condition of consent remains a condition when plans become inconvenient.
You can correct a vague answer before someone acts on an assumption.
A respectful conversation can end with no shared plan for sex.
ending_pause.reflection: Where did Jordan move from a hint or assumption to a clear condition? Which wording would feel natural for you?

ending_plan.title: A plan for a clearer conversation
ending_plan.summary: Jordan and Sam leave sex undecided and make room for another conversation. They can explore questions and conditions before considering a shared plan. Getting information or talking again creates no obligation to proceed.
takeaways: Explain your own needs without guessing another person's health status.
Reliable information can support a decision without making it for you.
A later discussion must leave room for different answers.
ending_plan.reflection: What is the difference between planning to discuss protection and agreeing to have sex?

ending_company.title: A movie is simply a movie
ending_company.summary: Jordan and Sam choose to spend time together with sex off the table. They have made a separate agreement about an activity they both want, and either can still end the evening. Jordan's protection boundary remains unchanged.
takeaways: An alternative activity should be freely wanted by both people.
Staying together does not imply consent to sex.
You do not need to abandon a condition to preserve connection.
ending_company.reflection: Which part of the conversation made the alternative activity a real choice rather than an expectation?
